items: The @Autowired annotation triggers theAutowiredAnnotationBeanPostProcessor, which inspects class metadata during bean initialization, resolving dependencies lazily or eagerly depending on container configuration.
@Qualifier metadata can be applied not just to standard bean names, but also to custom stereotype annotations, enabling powerful meta-annotation-driven configuration strategies.
When using JSR-330's @Inject, note that it does not support Spring's required = false attribute natively; instead, developers must inject an Optional<T> or ObjectProvider<T> wrapper.

@Resource resolution semantics dictate that if a name attribute is explicitly provided, it strictly searches for that specific bean name, bypassing type checks until the explicit lookup fails or type validation is enforced.

parsed_answer.content: A classic senior-level pitfall involves mixing @Autowired with field-level @Qualifier while attempting to mock dependencies in unit tests. Because field injection bypasses constructors, Mockito often struggles to inject mocks cleanly unless you use MockitoAnnotations.openMocks() or constructor-based injection. Always prefer constructor injection with @Qualifier parameters over field injection to maintain immutability and testability.
